objects.description: Opaque pointer type used by the FEC API to represent a forward-error-correction code instance created by fec_new(). The concrete struct/class is not defined in this header, so it must be treated as an opaque handle. Functions like fec_encode/fec_decode/get_k/get_n expect this pointer. Unknown internal layout and lifetime details beyond being created by fec_new() and freed by fec_free().

Pointer-to-pointer used throughout the RS/FEC API to pass arrays of data buffers: data[0..k-1] for sources and data[k..n-1] for parity. Although not a distinct typedef here, the API repeatedly uses char *data[] parameters to represent buffer vectors for encoding/decoding.

functions.name: fec_free
functions.description: Frees a FEC encoder/decoder context previously created with fec_new. Use to release resources when finished with a code instance.
requirements: p should be a pointer previously returned by fec_new (same library).
Do not use the code/context after calling fec_free (use-after-free).

functions.name: fec_new
functions.description: Creates and initializes a forward error correction (FEC) code context (likely Reed–Solomon over GF(2^GF_BITS)) for k data shards and n total shards (data + parity). The returned pointer is passed to other fec_* and rs_* APIs that require a code context.
requirements: n must be greater than or equal to k (as documented).
The caller must store and later pass the returned context pointer to other functions that require it (e.g., fec_encode, fec_decode, rs_encode, rs_decode).
init_fec is called automatically inside fec_new if it has not been called yet (no need to call it first).
Error handling behavior on allocation failure is not documented; returned pointer may be NULL or the function may abort — unknown.

functions.name: init_fec
functions.description: Initializes global/static tables needed for the FEC implementation. Normally you do not need to call this explicitly because fec_new will call it automatically if it hasn’t been called yet. Expose it only if you want to pre-initialize at program startup.
requirements: Safe to call before any other fec_* or rs_* calls to pre-initialize tables.
Not required to call before fec_new; fec_new will invoke it automatically if necessary.
Calling it multiple times should be safe or a no-op, but exact behavior is not documented — unknown.

functions.name: fec_encode
functions.signature: void fec_encode(void *code, void *src[], void *dst, int index, int sz)
functions.description: Encodes one shard/block using the provided FEC code context. Given an array of source data pointers, produces the encoded shard at the specified index and writes it into dst. Typically used to generate a specific parity shard of size sz bytes.
requirements: code must be a valid context returned by fec_new for the intended (k, n) code.
src must point to an array of pointers to at least k source shards; each referenced shard must contain at least sz bytes (exact layout unspecified — inferred).
dst must point to a writable buffer with capacity of at least sz bytes to receive the encoded shard (inferred).
index selects which output shard is computed; valid range and meaning (data vs parity) are not documented — unknown.
sz is the per-shard length in bytes and must match the size used consistently across corresponding encode/decode operations (inferred).

functions.name: fec_decode
functions.signature: int fec_decode(void *code, void *pkt[], int index[], int sz)
functions.description: Attempts to recover missing shards given a set of received packets and their corresponding original indices using the provided FEC context. Returns a status code; exact semantics are not documented.
requirements: code must be a valid context returned by fec_new for the matching (k, n) parameters.
pkt must be an array of pointers to shards of length at least sz bytes; missing shards may be represented by NULL pointers (not explicitly documented here — unknown).
index must be an array giving the original indices for the corresponding pkt entries; its length and valid value range are not documented — unknown.
sz must be the shard size in bytes and consistent with the encoding size (inferred).
Return value conventions (e.g., 0 on success) are not specified in this header — unknown.

functions.name: get_k
functions.description: Returns k (the number of data shards) from a FEC code context created by fec_new.
requirements: code must be a valid pointer previously returned by fec_new.

functions.name: get_n
functions.description: Returns n (the total number of shards: data + parity) from a FEC code context created by fec_new.
requirements: code must be a valid pointer previously returned by fec_new.

functions.name: rs_encode
functions.description: High-level Reed–Solomon encode helper using an existing FEC context. Given k original data blocks in data[0..k-1], generates n−k redundancy blocks and stores pointers in data[k..n-1]. The function will allocate memory for redundancy blocks and will exit the process on allocation failure.
requirements: code must be a valid fec_new-generated context whose k and n define the code parameters.
data must reference an array with capacity for at least n pointers.
data[0..k-1] must be non-NULL pointers to buffers of at least size bytes (original data).
size is the per-block length in bytes and must be consistent across all blocks in the operation.

The function may allocate memory for redundancy and store pointers into data[k..n-1]; callers must later free/manage those buffers according to the library’s lifecycle (exact ownership rules beyond allocation on encode are not documented).
On malloc failure the function will call exit(); callers should not expect a return in that case.

functions.name: rs_decode
functions.description: High-level Reed–Solomon decode/recovery using an existing FEC context. The input array data[0..n-1] contains pointers to data and redundancy blocks in proper order; set data[i] to NULL for missing blocks. On success, data[0..k-1] will be updated to point to the recovered original data. Returns 0 on success; returns non-zero if fewer than k non-NULL blocks are provided.
requirements: code must be a valid fec_new-generated context whose k and n define the code parameters.
data must reference an array of exactly n entries corresponding to indices 0..n−1.
Mark missing blocks by setting the corresponding data[i] pointer to NULL.
At least k entries in data[0..n−1] must be non-NULL, otherwise the function fails and returns non-zero.
size must be the per-block length in bytes and must match the size used during encoding.

The function will not malloc memory for NULL pointers in data[0..k−1]; instead, it will reuse memory from other non-NULL pointers and adjust data[0..k−1] to point at those buffers. After return, the total count of non-NULL pointers in data[0..n−1] remains unchanged (order and which entries are non-NULL may change).
Callers must not assume that original buffer ownership or positions are preserved; they should use the updated pointers after decoding.

functions.name: rs_encode2
functions.signature: void rs_encode2(int k, int n, char *data[], int size)
functions.description: High-level Reed–Solomon encode helper that takes k and n explicitly, without requiring a fec_new-generated context. Produces redundancy blocks for data[0..k-1] and stores them in data[k..n-1]. Specific allocation and failure behavior are not documented here; by analogy with rs_encode, it likely allocates redundancy buffers.
requirements: k and n define the code parameters; n must be >= k (inferred from the library’s overall contract).
data must reference an array with capacity for at least n pointers.
data[0..k-1] must be non-NULL pointers to buffers of at least size bytes (inferred).
size is the per-block length in bytes and must be consistent across all blocks (inferred).
Allocation strategy, error handling, and ownership for data[k..n-1] are not documented here — unknown.

functions.name: rs_decode2
functions.signature: int rs_decode2(int k, int n, char *data[], int size)
functions.description: High-level Reed–Solomon decode helper that takes k and n explicitly, without requiring a fec_new-generated context. Recovers original data into data[0..k-1] given at least k non-NULL blocks in data[0..n-1]. Return value semantics are not documented here; by analogy with rs_decode, it likely returns 0 on success and non-zero on failure.
requirements: k and n define the code parameters; n must be >= k (inferred).
data must reference an array of exactly n entries; set data[i] to NULL for missing blocks (inferred).
At least k entries in data[0..n−1] should be non-NULL to succeed (inferred).
size must be the per-block length in bytes and must match the encoder’s size (inferred).
Exact memory reuse behavior (like rs_decode’s reuse guarantee) and precise return codes are not documented — unknown.

data_types.description: Unstructured byte buffer of length specified by the caller. May contain any values 0x00–0xFF and is treated as opaque data by the FEC/Reed–Solomon routines. Used as shard/block contents; size is provided separately and callers must ensure buffers are at least that many bytes.
